payload.title: Experiment: kinetic friction coefficient from stopping distances

stimulus.description: A student gives a block a range of initial speeds $v_0$ along a level, rough table, measures the initial speed with a photogate, and measures the distance $d$ the block slides before it stops. The block and the table surface are the same in every trial.

notes: A student gives a block a range of initial speeds $v_0$ along a level, rough table, measures the initial speed with a photogate, and measures the distance $d$ the block slides before it stops. The block and the table surface are the same in every trial.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Describe an experimental procedure to collect the data for the stopping distance as a function of the initial speed. Include the equipment and the measurements, how the independent variable is changed, and one way to reduce the uncertainty in the measured distance.
parts.model_answer: Use a photogate (or motion sensor) to measure the initial speed and a meterstick to measure the sliding distance from the starting point to where the block stops; give the same block different initial speeds on the same table surface, and repeat each trial and average the distances.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies a way to measure the initial speed (photogate or motion sensor, or distance and time over a short interval) and a way to measure the stopping distance (meterstick or tape)
required_elements: a way to measure the initial speed and a way to measure the stopping distance
common_errors: omits how the speed is measured

rubric_rows.criterion: Changes only the initial speed while using the same block and the same table surface (both conditions are needed)
required_elements: change only the initial speed with the same block and surface

rubric_rows.criterion: Reduces the uncertainty in the distance by repeating each trial and averaging, or by marking the stopping point with a method that reduces the reading error (either earns the point)
required_elements: repeat and average or reduce the reading error (either earns the point)

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: Using the work-energy relationship for a block sliding to rest on a level surface with constant kinetic friction, identify the quantities that should be plotted on the vertical and horizontal axes so that the data produce a straight line whose slope can be used to find the coefficient of kinetic friction $\mu$.
parts.model_answer: From $\mu mgd=\tfrac12mv_0^2$ we get $d=\dfrac{1}{2\mu g}v_0^2$: plot $d$ on the vertical axis against $v_0^2$ on the horizontal axis; the slope is $1/(2\mu g)$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Identifies $d$ (vertical) versus $v_0^2$ (horizontal)
common_errors: plots d versus v0

parts.label: C
parts.prompt: On a blank grid whose scale you choose, plot the data in a form that gives a straight line, and draw a best-fit line. Label the axes with quantities and units and use a scale that fills most of the grid.

rubric_rows.criterion: Axes are labeled with quantities and units and the scale fills most of the grid
common_errors: scale uses less than half the grid

rubric_rows.criterion: Plots the five points $(v_0^2, d)$ accurately
Draws a straight best-fit line through the trend of the points
common_errors: connects the dots

parts.label: D
parts.prompt: Use the best-fit line to determine the coefficient of kinetic friction $\mu$. Show your work.
parts.model_answer: Slope $\approx 0.254\text{ s}^2/\text{m}$, so $\mu=\dfrac{1}{2g\,\text{slope}}\approx 0.20$.

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates the slope of the best-fit line using two points on the line (about 0.254 s^2/m; accept any value within 5 percent)
common_errors: uses data points rather than points on the line

rubric_rows.criterion: Relates the slope to the friction coefficient: slope $=1/(2\mu g)$
common_errors: uses slope = mu

rubric_rows.criterion: Calculates $\mu$ (about 0.20; accept any value within 8 percent); the coefficient has no units
alt_solutions: a value of mu consistent with the student's own slope from D1, $\mu=1/(2g\,\text{slope})$
